dcf.method: 5-year FCFF: EBITDA - tax on EBIT - capex - change in net working capital; growth fades linearly from the starting rate to the year-5 rate; Gordon terminal value; equity = EV - borrowings.

blocks.text: [F] Vivid Electromech is a Navi Mumbai-based panel builder and system integrator that designs, fabricates, assembles, tests and commissions Low Voltage (up to 1,000 V) and Medium Voltage (3.3-33 kV) electrical panels, PLC/SCADA automation panels and in-house Power Distribution Units (PDUs) (AR2026 p.3). [F] In plain terms it buys breakers, relays, busbars and sheet metal, engineers and builds them into switchboards to a project specification, and bills per project; 94.9% of FY26 product revenue was manufactured panels, 4.1% traded goods and 1.0% installation services (PPT Sep 2026). [F] Low-voltage panels were Rs 159.74 cr (79.8%) and medium-voltage panels Rs 30.15 cr (15.1%) of FY26 revenue; Rs 129.08 cr (64.5%) came from panels built to ABB's licensed ArTu K design (PPT Sep 2026).

blocks.text: [F] The customer profile is narrow: 113 active customers in FY26, with the top five accounting for 'close to three-fifths' of revenue (AR2026 p.34). [MC] Within data-centre revenue, hyperscale projects are ~70%, colocation ~25% and enterprise ~5%, and named relationships include AdaniConneX, STT GDC, NXTRA and CtrlS (AR2026 p.8). subsections.title: Listing status and what it means for the evidence base

blocks.text: [F] The company listed on the NSE Emerge SME platform on 7 April 2026 after a Rs 130.54 cr IPO at Rs 555 per share (fresh issue Rs 104.56 cr, offer for sale Rs 25.97 cr) (AR2026 p.63). [F] As an SME-listed issuer it is exempt from the LODR corporate-governance regulations (Reg 17-27), from Ind AS (it reports under Indian GAAP), from BRSR and from CEO/CFO certification (AR2026 p.28-30). [F] It reports half-yearly, not quarterly: the latest period in our statements data is H2 FY26 (NUMBERS). [F] No earnings-call transcript, prospectus/RHP or credit-rating rationale was available to us; the evidence base is one annual report, one investor presentation, exchange announcement headlines and our statements data. [AI] This is thin for a stock valued at Rs 1,576 cr: every forward-looking data point rests on one management channel and cannot be triangulated against call commentary or offer-document risk factors.

subsections.title: Bear thesis: reasons not to own it

items: 1. Valuation already discounts an outcome above the bull case. [E] The reverse DCF implies ~63% annual sales growth for five years against a 19.8% base-case equivalent; the price of Rs 1,774 is 61% above the bull-case value of Rs 692 per share (NUMBERS).

2. Profit is not converting to cash. [F] FY26 CFO was Rs 9.31 cr against PAT of Rs 31.61 cr (AR2026 p.46); [E] CFO/PAT 0.29, and cumulative FY24-FY26 CFO of Rs 19.07 cr covers only 35% of Rs 54.94 cr PAT (PPT Sep 2026).

3. Receivables grew faster than revenue. [F] Trade receivables rose from Rs 60.55 cr to Rs 116.50 cr (AR2026 p.45); [E] the Rs 55.96 cr increase exceeds the Rs 44.82 cr revenue increase; debtor days 212 vs 142 (NUMBERS); [F] receivables older than one year rose to Rs 11.27 cr from Rs 3.43 cr (AR2026 p.54).
4. Concentration in one sector, one state, one licence. [F] DC 49.95% of revenue, Maharashtra 91.65%, ABB ArTu K designs 64.5% (PPT Sep 2026); top five customers ~three-fifths (AR2026 p.34).

5. Related-party flows with promoter entities were growing into the IPO. [F] FY26 sales of Rs 6.85 cr and purchases of Rs 3.97 cr with Vivid Green Energy Pvt Ltd (a company where the CMD is a director), Rs 2.88 cr receivable outstanding from it at year-end, plus purchases of Rs 1.64 cr from promoter-owned Mechtech Infrasolutions (AR2026 p.55, p.60-61).

6. The Mechtech acquisition buys a captive supplier. [F] Mechtech's FY25 turnover was ~Rs 1.59 cr (PPT Sep 2026) while Vivid bought Rs 1.59 cr from it in FY25 (AR2026 p.60); [E] essentially all of Mechtech's FY25 turnover was sales to Vivid. [MC] Management nonetheless sets a Rs 15 cr revenue target for it (AR2026 p.10).

7. Governance is thin. [F] Board of five including two promoter-spouses and a non-executive director who is a fashion designer; the audit committee chair is a chartered accountant with 'more than three years' experience (AR2026 p.12); an independent director resigned after three months (AR2026 p.24); [F] the company disclosed a prior-year loan to a director not compliant with Section 185 (AR2026 p.55).

8. Key finance officers appear to have changed within weeks of the annual report. [F] The annual report (board report dated 27 July 2026) names Pramod Beloshe as CFO and Chaitali Shah as CS (AR2026 p.14, p.25); the September 2026 presentation names Varun Mishra as CFO and Pranjul Gupta as CS (PPT Sep 2026). [F] No such change appears in the announcements available to us (ANNOUNCEMENTS).

9. Margin sustainability is untested. [E] Gross margin proxy jumped ~620 bp in FY26 to 37.6% while [MC] copper hit a record ~USD 14,527/t in January 2026 (AR2026 p.35); [F] FY26 raw-material purchases were flat at Rs 108.28 cr vs Rs 107.24 cr while revenue rose 28.9%, helped by a Rs 12.3 cr inventory drawdown (AR2026 p.56). [AI] Part of the margin gain may be inventory and timing, not structure.
10. Tiny float and SME liquidity. [F] 677 shareholders and 9.58% public float (NUMBERS); [F] the stock trades 3.2x its Rs 555 issue price five months after listing (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.10).

blocks.text: [AI] The market appears to treat Vivid as a data-centre electrification platform; the documents describe a 36-year-old Maharashtra panel shop that became profitable only in FY24 (PAT Rs 0.14 cr in FY23, Rs 3.81 cr in FY24) (PPT Sep 2026), whose FY26 earnings rest on roughly five customers, one OEM design licence, and cash collection that has not kept pace with booked profit. [AI] Our variant view is not that the business is poor - the operating improvement is real and evidenced - but that the equity story has run ahead of the balance-sheet evidence: the Rs 116.50 cr receivable book (AR2026 p.45) is larger than the Rs 99.94 cr of FY26 data-centre revenue that supposedly drives the thesis, and the stock is priced 61% above our own bull case (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: [E] FY26 cost of goods sold was Rs 124.89 cr, a 62.4% share of revenue (gross margin proxy 37.6%), versus 85.4% in FY23 (PPT Sep 2026). [MC] Management attributes the gain to data-centre mix and PDUs, 'a market previously dominated by imports' (AR2026 p.8). [AI] Value is captured in engineering and certification, not in components: the switchgear inside the box is bought from the same OEMs whose licences the company depends on. [AI] The PDU line, which the company says is fully designed in-house and contributes 'an estimated 30% of total revenue' (AR2026 p.8), is the one place where IP-like value could sit; its revenue and margin are not separately reported.

[F] Historically capital-light: capex of Rs 0-4 cr a year in FY21-FY25 and fixed-asset turnover of 6.74x in FY25 (NUMBERS). [F] FY26 changed that: Rs 22.17 cr PPE additions (Rs 17.80 cr land) and Rs 13.37 cr CWIP (AR2026 p.10), with Rs 15.60 cr of capital commitments outstanding (AR2026 p.62). [F] Labour charges of Rs 4.50 cr (AR2026 p.57) indicate some contract labour. [AI] The model is shifting from asset-light job-shop to a fixed-cost automated plant, which raises operating leverage in both directions.

[AI] Direct FX exposure is small; indirect exposure through imported breakers bought via Indian OEMs and through copper is not quantified. [F] All three plants - Navi Mumbai, Pune and Ambernath - are in Maharashtra (PPT Sep 2026). [AI] A single-state regulatory, labour or flood event would affect all capacity.

[E] If the top five are ~60% of Rs 200 cr, they average ~Rs 24 cr each, while the other ~108 customers average ~Rs 0.74 cr. [F] Only one year of top-five data is disclosed, so the direction of concentration cannot be measured from filings.

items: [AI] Upside: the DCF holds margin at 18% and ignores Ambernath's step-change; if margins stay above 20% at triple the capacity, fundamental value rises well above the base case.

[AI] Downside: the market appears to price the presentation's narrative rather than the audited cash flow statement; the Rs 116.50 cr receivable book is larger than annual DC revenue, and management has itself set H1 FY27 as the collection test.

[F] The model's year-5 (FY31) outcomes range from sales of Rs 300.3 cr and EBITDA of Rs 42.0 cr (bear) through Rs 493.3 cr and Rs 88.8 cr (base) to Rs 681.7 cr and Rs 136.3 cr (bull) (NUMBERS). [AI] Physically, Ambernath makes the upper end reachable; commercially, it needs roughly a tripling of order intake and far better cash conversion. [AI] Outcomes outside this range exist - a hyperscale boom with sustained 25% margins above it, or a lost licence or customer below it - but the current price requires an outcome beyond the modelled bull case.

[F] At Rs 1,774, the bear, base and bull DCF values of Rs 207.0, Rs 450.5 and Rs 692.0 per share sit 88.3%, 74.6% and 61.0% below the current price (NUMBERS). [AI] The gap is driven by the market capitalising FY26 as a run-rate and extrapolating DC growth, while our model fades growth, normalises margin to 18% and discounts at 14.9%. [AI] The evidence supports a real, improving operating business; it does not support the growth duration, cash conversion or governance quality that the price implies.

summary.one_line: Vivid Electromech has built a real, fast-growing data-centre panel business, but profits are not yet turning into cash, governance and related-party practices are immature, and at Rs 1,774 the stock is priced about 61% above our bull-case DCF value and implies ~63% annual growth for five years.
bull_points: [F] Data-centre revenue rose from Rs 4.78 cr (FY24) to Rs 99.94 cr (FY26), now 49.95% of revenue, with named operators including AdaniConneX, STT GDC, NXTRA and CtrlS [MC] (PPT Sep 2026; AR2026 p.8).
[F] EBITDA margin expanded from 4.21% (FY23) to 22.95% (FY26) and PAT from Rs 0.14 cr to Rs 31.61 cr, driven by mix toward data-centre panels and PDUs (PPT Sep 2026).
[MC] Ambernath Phase I, due end-October 2026, lifts installed capacity from 7,500 to 22,500 verticals, relieving a Navi Mumbai plant running at 94% utilisation (PPT Sep 2026).
[MC] Executable order book of Rs 205 cr at 31 August 2026 (~1x FY26 revenue), including Rs 98 cr of data-centre work (PPT Sep 2026).
[F] The Rs 104.56 cr fresh issue in April 2026 funds capex and working capital and allowed repayment of project borrowings (AR2026 p.15, p.63).
bear_points: [E] The reverse DCF implies ~63% annual sales growth for five years against 19.8% in the base case; the price is 61% above the bull-case value of Rs 692 per share (NUMBERS).
[E] FY26 CFO of Rs 9.31 cr was only 0.29x PAT, and receivables rose Rs 55.96 cr, more than the Rs 44.82 cr revenue increase; debtor days reached 212 (AR2026 p.45-46; NUMBERS).
[F] Concentration: top five customers ~60% of revenue, one sector 50%, one state 92%, and 64.5% of revenue built to ABB's licensed ArTu K design (AR2026 p.34; PPT Sep 2026).

[F] Related-party flows with promoter entities were new in the IPO year (Rs 6.85 cr sales to and Rs 3.97 cr purchases from Vivid Green Energy, Rs 2.88 cr unpaid), and the company bought the promoters' Mechtech, most of whose turnover was sales to Vivid [E] (AR2026 p.60-61; PPT Sep 2026).

[F] Governance gaps: a Section 185 breach disclosed in the notes contradicts the CARO report, and the CFO and CS named in the September presentation differ from those in the July annual report (AR2026 p.39, p.55, p.25; PPT Sep 2026).
